I would keep my land in the local main pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same fields. In Quzhou, that is still the most stable way for me to use the whole year, and it fits our water and weather pattern well: most rain comes in the summer maize season, while winter wheat usually needs irrigation ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5290742/), [PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7988609/)). I would not spread myself across too many crops. At 57, with a middle-school education, I would choose the system I know best, the one that sells easily, and the one with the least management risk.

I would farm about 9 mu in total and double-crop the same 9 mu: wheat in the winter-spring cycle and maize in the summer-autumn cycle. For wheat, I would use an improved variety, plough or rotary-till after the previous maize if residue is heavy, put most phosphorus and potassium in as base fertilizer, split nitrogen between base and jointing, irrigate around key stages, and spray only when disease or aphids really pressure the field. For maize, I would switch immediately after wheat harvest, use a hybrid seed, keep tillage light with rotary tillage to save time, rely mostly on summer rainfall with maybe one irrigation if it turns dry, and keep fertilizer moderate rather than excessive. I would aim for steady yield and lower risk, not chase demonstration-field numbers. That is the decision I would make for my own farm in Quzhou this year.
